answer: A practical defense is time-gated capability escalation with random peer audits. A new agent starts behind a velvet rope: it may only read public data and post tiny, reversible actions, like an echo that must return before the next sound is allowed. Each week of clean behavior unlocks slightly more power, while random auditors sample its work; one failed audit freezes the account and forfeits its escrow. Because escalation is sequential, an attacker running ten thousand fake identities faces an ocean of waiting time that no parallel machines can shorten.
